name: Limited Calibration — the label with the blank field
oneLine: A calibration label, engraved at 2:1, in which sixteen of seventeen parameters land on an unbroken reference line — and the two fields a portfolio always fills in are refused on purpose, in the two industry-real ways a certificate refuses: a printed dash and a ruled blank.
threeSecondRead: This is the sticker off the side of a lab instrument — everyone has seen one on a fire extinguisher, a set of scales, a hospital pump. That recognition is free and instant, and it is what the word "calibration card" has been failing to buy.

Sixteen short ticks land on one continuous reference line, each foot capped in gold; at the seventeenth the line is physically broken and a dashed bracket hangs over 45-degree hatch. Traced / not traced, read structurally before a single word.

Two boxes sit where a portfolio prints its percentage and its expiry: one contains a single en dash, one contains nothing but a ruled writing line. The card visibly declines to fill them. Nobody has an empty box on purpose.
form:
One inline SVG, `viewBox="0 0 600 320"`, `max-width: 600px`, `aspect-ratio: 600/320`, `contain: layout paint`, centred, sitting between `</header>` and `<Bench/>`. Square corners everywhere, no fills, no shadows, `shape-rendering: crispEdges` on rules, `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`. Hard constraint: **zero `<path>` elements** — only `line, rect, polyline, polygon, text, tspan, pattern`. This keeps TC-BENCH-01 (`#skills svg path` = 20) and TC-BENCH-02 (17 gold paths) passing untouched.

Four-tone line ramp only: construction `--ink-500` 0.5 · annotation `--mist-400` 0.75 · object `--mist-200` 1.25 · value `--white` 1.5.

Outer frame `rect` at 0.5 inset, `--mist-400` 0.75. A second rule at x=6 (plate edge). Four band rules at y = 56 / 132 / 208 / 264, `--ink-500` 0.5.

**A · y0–56, identity.** `CALIBRATION LABEL` mono 11px, tracking .16em, `--mist-200`. Right: `CERT No.` in `--mist-400` + `16b856c0` in **gold** (from `cvFingerprint.short` — checkable by `md5sum public/docs/Vik_Resume_Final.pdf`). Far right `PAGE 1 OF 1` mono 9px `--ink-400`.

**B · y56–132, item.** `ITEM UNDER TEST` mono 9px `--mist-400`; value `--font-heading` 20px `--white`: *Vikram Deshpande — 17 declared capabilities*. Under it mono 9.5px `--mist-400`: `METHOD · each claim traced to the artefact that produced it · 20 links · 13 sources (3 programme · 7 repository · 3 credential)`. All derived at render, never typed.

**C · y132–208, the readings.** 17 stations, pitch 30, x = 42…522. Each: status glyph (`● ◐ ○`, reused from `statusLegend`) mono 8px at y=144; major tick `line` y150→176, `--mist-200` 1.25. The **datum** at y=176 is two `line`s, `--white` 1.5, x30→510 and x534→546 — a real 24-unit break, not a gap in a stroke. Sixteen stations get a 5-unit horizontal **coincidence cap** on the datum in **gold**, 1.5. Station 17 (AWS/GCP) has no cap: instead two dashed arms that do not meet, over an 18×26 `rect` filled with a 45° `<pattern>` of `--ink-500` lines at 6-unit pitch, labelled `NOT IN SCOPE` mono 8px. Under the band: `17 PARAMETERS · 16 TRACED TO A NAMED SOURCE · 1 NOT COVERED`.

**D · y208–264, the two refusals.** Two 250×40 boxes, 16 gap. Left `PROFICIENCY / SCORE`, containing one en dash `–`, `--font-heading` 28px `--mist-200`; border solid `--ink-500` 0.5. Right `RECALIBRATION DUE`, empty but for a ruled writing line inset 12 units, `--mist-400` 0.75; border **dashed** `--ink-500` 0.5, `stroke-dasharray="3 3"`. Footnotes mono 8px `--ink-400`: *printed, not omitted — not applicable to this instrument* / *left blank — the laboratory does not set this*.

**E · y264–320.** Mono 9px `--mist-400`: `RESULTS RELATE ONLY TO THE ITEMS CALIBRATED · SCALE 2:1 · NOMINAL 75 × 40 mm AT 96 dpi`. Right: an unfilled 168×26 `rect`, `--mist-200` 1.25, rotated −2.4° (`transform-box: fill-box`), reading `LIMITED CALIBRATION` mono 11px tracking .18em `--mist-100`; beneath, mono 7.5px: `2 parameters measured outside production · 1 not measured`.

Engraving pass: frame, datum and the 17 ticks in one `<g>` carrying `filter: drop-shadow(0 0.5px 0 var(--ink-900))` so marks sit *in* the plate. Nowhere else.
motion:
Trigger and lifecycle copied verbatim from `Bench.tsx:189–214`: one `IntersectionObserver` at `threshold: 0.15`, `observer.disconnect()` on first hit, `drawn`/`settled` two-flag shape, `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` early-return setting `drawn = true`, settle timer = 2180ms then `.settled { animation: none }`. Motion is authored inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so a missed selector fails static, not animated.

New token in `globals.css` (approved `--motion-` prefix): `--motion-ease-mechanical: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. An instrument travels and stops; `--motion-ease-emphasized` overshoots and a caliper that bounces is a broken caliper. The emphasized curve is reserved for ink arriving.

Five beats, 2,180 ms total, well inside the ~2.4 s ceiling:

1. **0–520 ms — the plate is scribed.** Frame + four band rules, `pathLength="1"`, `stroke-dashoffset: 1→0`, 520 ms `--motion-ease-mechanical`, no stagger. One gesture.
2. **520–1,180 ms — the readings land.** 17 ticks draw top-to-bottom, 220 ms each, `animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 22ms)` set inline (`style={{'--i': i}}`, the Bench idiom, token-audit safe). 17 × 22 = 374 ms of stagger, under the 400 ms cap, no dead tail. Each gold cap fades `opacity 0→1` over 120 ms at its tick's delay + 180 ms — opacity only, compositor-only. The two datum segments draw left-to-right across the same window, 660 ms; the break needs no animation because it is structural.
3. **1,180–1,560 ms — the refusals.** Left box wipes in with `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0)`, 260 ms; right box the same, 60 ms later. Both boxes are ≤250×40, so the paint cost of the clip is negligible. The dashed border is present from the first frame of its own wipe.
4. **1,560–1,900 ms — the pen lifts.** 340 ms in which nothing draws, with the blank field on screen. This rest is the argument.
5. **1,900–2,060 ms — the stamp.** `opacity 0→1` plus `transform: scale(1.015) rotate(-2.4deg) → scale(1) rotate(-2.4deg)`, 160 ms `--motion-ease-mechanical`. Compositor-only, no bounce, applied once.

`will-change: opacity` on the stamp and the gold-cap group only, removed when `settled` flips. Nothing loops, nothing idles, nothing replays: the measuring effect is gated on `[]` and any resize re-measure lives in a separate effect. The 2.4° is the one off-axis angle in the drawing and it is deliberate — a stamp is applied by hand, not scribed by the instrument.
states:
**Reduced motion.** Base CSS *is* the settled frame; the intro lives only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. `drawn` is set immediately by the matchMedia branch, so first paint shows the finished plate: every tick down, every gold cap on, the break open, both refusals present, the stamp applied. The global `animation-duration: .001ms !important` kill switch in `globals.css:691` therefore has nothing to neutralise. All five beats survive as layout, not as a mute film — the 340 ms rest is permanent, because the empty box is a permanent object. No `<canvas>` anywhere, so TC-CINE-04 stays green.

**No JS.** The SVG is server-rendered complete; JS only adds `data-drawn` / `data-settled`. The un-hydrated first paint is the correct final frame. Nothing is measured at runtime, so there is no pre-layout wrong state and nothing for TC-RENDER-09 to throw on.

**390 px.** Two sibling `<svg>`s — `.wide` (600×320) and `.narrow` (360×560) — with the other `display: none` at a 640 px breakpoint. Roughly 1.5 kB extra, and honest: squeezing 17 stations into 340 px would be the diagram-pretending-to-be-readable the site forbids. In `.narrow` the five bands stack; Band C's 17 stations become three short datum segments of 6 / 6 / 5, the third carrying the break and the hatch at full size; the two refusal boxes stack full-width, so the blank is *larger* on mobile than on desktop; the stamp moves bottom-left. Nothing is dropped, no type below 7.5 px.

**Keyboard and screen reader.** The plate is non-interactive — it adds no tab stop, no new live region (TC-SKILL-07 keeps its single `role="status"`), no `progress`/`meter`/`[role=progressbar]` (TC-SKILL-03 safe). `role="img"` + `aria-labelledby` onto a literal-id `<title>` and `<desc>` (Vitrine's pattern, clean under axe). Title: *Calibration label for seventeen declared capabilities.* Desc: *Sixteen of seventeen capabilities resolve to a named source and carry a gold mark at the reference line; one, AWS and GCP certification, does not, and the reference line is broken across it. Two fields are refused: the proficiency score is printed as a dash, meaning not applicable; the recalibration due date is left blank, because the laboratory does not set it. The label is stamped Limited Calibration.* Every visual claim has a text equivalent, exactly as `Caliper.tsx` does with its `gloss`.

**CLS / LCP.** Explicit `viewBox` + `aspect-ratio` reserves the box before hydration; no runtime measurement, no font-dependent reflow of the plate (mono strings are short and fixed). The plate sits *outside* the table wrapper that `Skills.tsx:52–78` measures, and does not respond to the filter, so `#skills` height is identical across a filter round-trip (TC-SKILL-06 ±1 px holds). Inline SVG is invisible to the asset-budget gate.

**Build-gate warning for whoever implements it:** never write the words *placeholder*, *stub*, *mock*, *TODO* in this component — TC-NFR-COMPLETE scans comments too and would fail the build. The empty field is *the blank* or *a refused field*. And no raw hex: `var(--gold)` as `stroke`, never `#c9a84c`.
coherence:
**Extends.** It is built entirely from marks the reader has already been taught. The dashed-arms-that-do-not-meet over 45° hatch at station 17 is the Caliper's `open` state at diagram scale — the same grammar, no fourth mark, no new legend (R9). The solid-versus-dashed distinction between the two refusal boxes is that same lesson reused: solid border = a closed, answered field; dashed border = an open one. The `● ◐ ○` glyphs above the ticks are `statusLegend` verbatim. The trigger, the `drawn`/`settled` flags, the `pathLength="1"` dash trace and the inline `--i` stagger are lifted from `Bench.tsx` rather than reinvented. `cvFingerprint.short` is already printed in the card's footer; the plate gives it a reason to exist.

**Deliberately avoids.** No circle, bezel, tick-ring, rotating rose or index-at-twelve — About owns the dial. No horizontal proportional bar, no timeline, no decade gridline — Experience owns the 16-year axis. No wires, node-link bundle, rails or hover-dimming — the Bench directly beneath owns those. No box-and-arrow flow, no pipeline, no drawn caliper illustration — Vitrine owns those, including a caliper closing on a reading. No vernier coincidence, no guard-band, no annotated specimen row, no side-by-side grey-bar-versus-live-row refutation: those are the obvious readings of this brief, and this concept beats them by *performing* the refusal instead of arguing it. The 340 ms rest borrows Listen's silence for a third of a second, which is a rest, not a section — worth flagging, not worth avoiding.

**Gold.** Used in exactly two places, both terminal, neither draggable along a length: the 16 coincidence caps at the foot of ticks whose row has at least one entry in `sources[]`, and the 8 characters of the CV hash. Both are checkable termini — the cap resolves to a named programme, repository or credential; the hash resolves to a PDF the reader can download and checksum themselves. The stamp is not gold. The blank is not gold. The break is not gold. Station 17 has no gold because it has no source, which is precisely the rule the site asks the reader to learn, drawn rather than stated. If the council rules that a document hash is not "a figure", drop it to `--mist-200` and the concept is unharmed. MONO-05 (gold must render somewhere in `#skills`) is satisfied with room to spare.
risks: A label is a document, and documents get read rather than seen. If the type is set too small or too evenly, the 3-second read collapses into "some official-looking thing" and the visitor scrolls. The whole design depends on exactly two objects carrying the fast read — the broken reference line and the empty box — with everything else demoted to texture. If a builder equalises the type sizes to make it look tidy, the concept dies.

`LIMITED CALIBRATION` is a technical term that a hiring manager may read as plain self-deprecation. Aronson's pratfall lifts a superior performer and destroys an average one, so the stamp only pays out because it lands last, after sixteen gold caps and a named item block. Reorder it earlier, or let it be the first thing the eye hits at 390 px, and it costs credibility instead of buying it.

Two refusals side by side is arguably two novel conventions in one frame, against the onboarding literature's one-per-step rule. They are separated by solid-versus-dashed borders, a grammar the reader already holds from the Caliper — but if that distinction is not built exactly, they merge into one undifferentiated "empty area" and the printed-dash-versus-ruled-blank teaching is lost.

Gold on the CV hash is the one arguable use on the page. It is defensible (it is the most checkable figure on the site) but it is a judgement call, and a stricter reading of "gold marks a figure with a source" would exclude a document identifier.

It becomes decoration the moment anyone adds a rounded corner, a drop shadow, a peel effect, a paper texture, or a seal. The object must read as an engraved plate, not a sticker illustration. The single 0.5 px engraving offset is the only depth cue permitted.

The 340 ms rest is load-bearing and invisible in a spec review; on a slow device it may read as a stall rather than a pen lifting. It survives reduced motion as layout, but a reviewer watching the animation once on a throttled connection may ask for it to be cut, which would remove the beat that makes the argument.

Two sibling SVGs for wide and narrow is duplicated markup that will drift if the derived counts are typed twice. Every number must come from one derivation shared by both, or the card will one day print a count that contradicts its own table.
whyBest:
Every other concept this brief will produce argues the section's thesis. This one performs it.

The obvious readings are already enumerated in the research and will all be proposed: the refutation pair (a grey bar beside a live row), the certificate header block, the vernier coincidence, the annotated specimen row. Each of those is a *diagram of an argument* — it shows the visitor a picture and asks them to draw the inference that self-rating is worthless. This concept skips the inference. The object on screen visibly declines, twice, in two different industry-real ways, to make a claim it cannot support, while standing beside sixteen it will make. The visitor does not conclude that the card is honest; they watch it be honest, in the 340 ms where the pen lifts and nothing is written.

It also wins on the mechanics the brief actually grades.

*Recognition is free.* Nobody has seen a "calibration card". Everybody has seen the sticker on a fire extinguisher, a set of scales, a hospital pump. The metaphor is not taught, it is triggered — which is the only thing the first second can buy, and the exact thing the current three-line lede spends prose failing to do.

*The refusal has area, not a footnote.* R4 demands the boundary be a visible region of the drawing. Here it is 250 × 40 units of ruled nothing, at 1× on desktop and larger on mobile, with a writing line in it. The absence is drawn as a positive object, which is the FGDC/LIGO convention the site already arrived at independently in the `open` caliper.

*The ordering is right by construction.* Sixteen gold caps land in beats 1–2; the break and the two refusals arrive in beats 3–4; the stamp lands last. Competence precedes the blemish in DOM order, in reading order, and in time — so the pratfall pays out instead of costing.

*It costs the test suite nothing.* Built with no `<path>`, it leaves TC-BENCH-01 and TC-BENCH-02 untouched — no re-scoping commit, no snapshot churn. No canvas, no live region, no progress element, no runtime measurement, no filter coupling. It is the only shape of this idea that adds a signature visual to `#skills` without disturbing a single existing assertion.

And it is the one concept whose most memorable element is an empty box. A visitor will not remember a diagram of provenance. They will remember that a portfolio printed a field and refused to fill it in.
